findings.title: Small-action edit/delete buttons lose right alignment once `.small-action` becomes a flex container
findings.body:
`.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but its layout still assumes block flow.

- **Buttons are direct children:** browsers ignore `float` on flex items, so `button { float: right; }` does nothing. The buttons render in source order, next to the avatar.
- **Buttons are inside `.small-action-desc`:** that element is now a flex item with the default `flex: 0 1 auto`. It shrinks to its content width instead of filling the row as the old block did (old padding-left was 4em). The right-floated buttons then sit right after the description text, not at the right edge of the post.

Either way, the edit/delete controls on small-action posts move visually. Fix by giving `.small-action-desc` `flex: 1` (and/or wrapping the buttons and pushing them right with `margin-left: auto`). The leftover `float` rules on `.topic-avatar` and `button` are dead code.

findings.title: Panel right-alignment depends on `margin-left: auto`, which the legacy box model these prefixes target doesn't honor
findings.body:
`float: right` was removed from `.d-header .panel`. Right-alignment now relies only on `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container.

The new `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits the 2009 `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` syntax for old browsers (old Android browser, older iOS Safari). In that box model, auto margins do not absorb free space. Those browsers will place the notification/user icons right after the logo and topic info instead of at the right edge of the header.

Either drop the legacy fallbacks so the support claim is honest, or add a legacy-compatible mechanism, e.g. a `-webkit-box-flex: 1` spacer or `-webkit-box-pack`.

findings.title: `order` / `align-items` mixins pass modern values verbatim to legacy properties with different value spaces
findings.body:
**`order($val)`:** `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` only accept integers >= 1, and their default is 1. Standard `order` defaults to 0 and allows 0 and negatives. So `order(0)` or a negative value produces an invalid legacy declaration. `order(1)` reorders an element in modern browsers but leaves it unchanged in legacy ones.

**`align-items($alignment)`:** it forwards values to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which use `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. `align-items(flex-start)` would emit invalid legacy declarations.

The current call sites (2, 3, `center`, `baseline`) happen to work. But these are generic shared mixins, and future callers will silently get inconsistent ordering or alignment. Map the values (e.g. ordinal-group = order + 1, flex-start → start) or document the restriction.

Separately, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property.

findings.title: `.extra-info-wrapper` as a flex item may not shrink for long topic titles
findings.body:
Before, `.extra-info-wrapper` sat in normal flow between the floated `.title` and `.panel`, so it naturally took the remaining width. Now it is a flex item (`order: 2`) with default `flex: 0 1 auto` and `min-width: auto`.

A flex item's automatic minimum size is its min-content width. For a header topic title rendered with `white-space: nowrap` and `text-overflow: ellipsis`, that is the full title width, so the item will not shrink below it. Long titles can then overflow the header and push `.panel` (search/notification/user icons) off-screen.

Unless `overflow: hidden` is guaranteed on this element elsewhere, add `min-width: 0` (or `overflow: hidden`) and an explicit flex basis so truncation keeps working.
